method: The hour hand turns 0.5 degrees a minute and the minute hand 6 degrees a minute, both clockwise from 12, so a time H:M:S puts the hour hand at 30 x H + 0.5 x M + S/120 degrees and the minute hand at 6 x M + 0.1 x S degrees. The angle between them is the difference taken the shorter way round, so it is never more than 180 degrees and the long way round is 360 degrees minus it. Because the minute hand gains 5.5 degrees a minute, the gap changes at 11/120 degrees a second, and the times when it equals a target A solve (11/120) x t = +/- A modulo 360, giving two moments an hour, 22 in the 12-hour cycle, except at 0 and 180 degrees where the two families coincide and there are 11. Hours are read on a 12-hour face, so 15:15 and 03:15 give the same reading and the listed times repeat twice a day. This models an ideal continuously moving face: it does not allow for a ticking movement, a stopped clock or the equation of time.
